summary: This resolution sets special floor procedures for House consideration of four measures—FY2026 DHS appropriations (H.R. 8029), a resolution supporting DHS (H. Res. 1128), a DC beautification commission bill (H.R. 5103), and a bill restricting foreign vessels in U.S. waters (H.R. 7084)—by waiving points of order, deeming specified amendments adopted, limiting debate to one hour, and allowing one motion to recommit on each.

scores.thoughts: The resolution provides procedural rules for considering H.R. 8029, an appropriations bill for DHS. While it facilitates debate on government spending, the resolution itself contains no substantive provisions directing or altering spending levels, making any connection procedural rather than substantive.
The resolution text makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions in the resolution address healthcare policy, coverage, or funding mechanisms.
The resolution contains no language related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The resolution enables consideration of DHS appropriations and a supportive resolution for DHS, an agency central to border enforcement. However, the resolution itself is strictly procedural and does not enact or direct any immigration policy changes.
No content in the resolution pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
DHS appropriations are referenced, but DHS is a civilian agency; the resolution does not engage military or defense spending.
H.R. 5103 on beautifying DC is mentioned, but the resolution provides only procedural rules and does not advance environmental policy.
The resolution text has no bearing on welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The resolution does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No engagement with sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform appears in the text.
H.R. 7084 concerns vessel operations in U.S. waters, which could touch trade logistics, but the resolution is purely procedural and does not set trade policy.
While an appropriations bill is referenced, the resolution itself neither authorizes deficit spending nor prioritizes debt reduction.
The resolution contains no provisions affecting LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No references to foreign aid or international assistance programs exist in the text.
The resolution does not address voting access, election procedures, or voter ID requirements.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The resolution makes no mention of labor rights, unions, or employment regulations.
No content addresses religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
